text:
maria: seeing a new latency cluster on prod pods around 15:10 UTC. correlates with high KV eviction pressure on long-context streams. logs show a lot of "deferred_reclaim" events and CPU spikes in pager threads.

devon: can you paste the exact log lines? which model/instance?

maria: paste below (sanitized):
```
2026-03-18T15:09:57Z pager[pid=8142] INFO evict: policy=FIFO pressure=0.92 deferred_reclaim=124 reclaim_ms=2.3
2026-03-18T15:10:01Z pager[pid=8142] WARN reclaim_queue_len=987 latency_p50=48ms latency_p95=310ms
2026-03-18T15:10:03Z runtime[pid=8001] ERROR long_context_stream id=78ab kv_page_fault=1 reuse_hit=false
```
streams are primarily long-context chat (seq_len ~12k tokens). only hosts running small A100 pools.

sanjay: hmm. FIFO under severe pressure + deferred reclaim backlog rings a bell. We added deferred reclaim to avoid stall in hot-path, but backlog can cause latency when pager threads eventually drain with big batches.

olivia: is FIFO correctness impacted? i.e., are we accidentally evicting in-use KV entries and causing re-fetch churn?

devon: from logs reuse_hit=false suggests eviction then immediate miss. but need trace to assert race vs expected miss. can you capture a KV trace for a single stream where p95 jumps?

maria: started an instrumented run on a repro cluster (same sequences). attaching short repro seq and the mini tracer output:
```
> repro: seed=42 model=xl-long context=12000 tokens
TRACE: evict_attempt id=0x1a23 key=ctx:78ab state=HOT->EVICTING owner_thread=worker-7
TRACE: deferred_reclaim enqueue id=0x1a23 size=4096
TRACE: worker-7 accessed key=ctx:78ab at t+12ms -> miss
TRACE: reclaim drained id=0x1a23 at t+220ms -> reinsert
```

sanjay: that trace is classic deferred-reclaim window too long. worker evicted a still-referenced slab then other worker noticed miss before reclaim -> reinsert -> churn

devon: two separate problems then: correctness (we should never evict an item still in use) and latency (reclaim batching/ordering creates spikes when backlog drains).

olivia: correctness: we previously relied on per-key refcounts + turnstile flag. if deferred_reclaim doesn't re-check refcount on drain, reinsert can violate invariants. code snippet from current pager:
```
if (should_defer(entry)) enqueue(deferred_queue, entry);
// later
while (pop(deferred_queue, entry)) {
  if (!entry->is_free()) reclaim(entry);
}
```
I think that second check is inverted: should be "if (entry->is_free()) reclaim" not the negation.

maria: confirmed: current code calls reclaim when not free -> we were reclaiming entries still in use. patch incoming.

devon: nice catch. that'll fix correctness and reduce churn. for latency, we should also avoid draining huge batches on the pager thread during critical paths. suggestions:
- cap per-iteration reclaim count (e.g., 32)
- exponential backoff for reclaim when queue grows
- prioritize entries by eviction_time to avoid reinsert hot keys

sanjay: also add metrics: deferred_queue_len, reclaim_batch_size, reinsert_count, forced_miss_rate by key-hotness.

olivia: can we try switching a single node to LRU variant (it tends to be better for reuse) and compare? i've got a bench harness to simulate reuse patterns.

maria: running A/B now: node-3 FIFO current, node-4 LRU. initial run (10m) shows node-3 p95=280ms, node-4 p95=72ms. interesting.

devon: that aligns: FIFO with our deferred pipeline was worse. LRU reduces evicting recently used slices. but LRU has higher bookkeeping cost under heavy write churn. measure CPU vs latency tradeoff.

olivia: also trying micro-optimizations: check-before-enqueue (peek refcount without locking) and small reclamation thresholds for long contexts.

maria: created PR with correctness fix + metrics + a configurable reclaim_batch cap. PR: https://git.redwood/infer/pull/5421 (CI failing on one flake)

ci-bot: build 5421/7 failed: unit-test kv_pager_queue_test::handles_race - retrying

devon: once PR merges can we roll to canary (10% traffic) and watch deferred_queue_len, reinsert_count, p95? If numbers fall, roll.

sanjay: add an alert: if reinsert_count > 1000/min AND deferred_queue_len > 500 -> paging-surge incident.

maria: I'll run canary in 30m and post metrics. thanks all. :thumbsup:

olivia: nice debugging flow. follow-ups: (1) validate LRU vs FIFO perf curve under different seq_len distributions, (2) add unit test for deferred reclaim mis-check, (3) consider probabilistic eviction under extreme pressure.

devon: noted. I'll own the canary and rollback plan.

maria: last: tagging infra to reserve extra memory headroom for the pool during test to avoid compounding OOMs: @ryan can you bump node mem by 10% in canary config?

ryan: done. bumped to 110% memory reservation for canary group.

maria: thanks — will report back with numbers. thread closed once canary stabilizes.
